newsitem.title: USA: EDS sees Q2 EPS $0.43 to $0.45 before charge.
newsitem.headline: EDS sees Q2 EPS $0.43 to $0.45 before charge.

text.p: Electronic Data Systems Corp said Monday at a meeting of security analysts that it estimated it would achieve earnings per share of $0.43 to $0.45 in the second quarter before adjusting for a previously announced, non-recurring restructuring charge of between $100 million and $250 million.
The company also said that it expects those restructuring efforts to provide potential annual savings of between $500 million and $700 million.
EDS also said that it was comfortable with an earlier estimate that 1997 earnings would range between $2.30 and $2.35 per share, before the special charge.
The company said that it expects earnings to improve in the second half of the year as the result of both cost-cutting efforts and the extensive global market opportunities available to the company.

EDS officials emphasized to the analysts at the meeting that it has had three consecutive quarters of strong new-contract signings and already has won more than $2 billion in new business in the second quarter.

EDS said its strategy for A.T. Kearney, the global management consulting firm it acquired in September 1995, was realizing synergies and benefits faster than anticipated and that A.T. Kearney is expected to register fees in excess of $1 billion this year.

The company's CIO Services 2000 group, which will help prepare computers for the new millennium, expects to add 400 positions in the next several months and additional 1,000 positions in 1998, said the company. The group reports a $1 billion-plus business pipeline as enterprises begin to move aggressively to solve their "Year 2000" problem.

The market acceptance of EDS's interactive agency for strategy design and development of websites for interactive marketing, c2o Interactive Architects, has been exceptional and has created business opportunities in the $400-million range in only four months, the company said. EDS estimates its total current pipeline in the area of Internet and new media at $1.75 billion.
